transcript:
Header: 2026-06-15 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Markus Reed (Silverline Head of ML), Priya Desai (VP Eng), Tom Alvarez (Cloud Architect), Sophie Nguyen (Procurement)

Summary: Quick renewal/expansion check-in after their usage spike in May. Discussed capacity increase, adding EU region, contract term options, and security artifacts. Decided next steps: pricing options, perf benchmarks, infra diagram, and procurement timeline.

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, uh, appreciate it. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Markus: Markus here.
[00:08] Priya: Priya on.
[00:09] Tom: Tom here.
[00:10] Sophie: Sophie joining.
[00:12] Jamie: Great, we've got Ravi and Lena from our side too. The goal for today is renewal and expansion options — I know you had a big spike in May and some latency issues for EU customers, plus procurement wants upcoming contract terms. Is that right, Markus?
[00:26] Markus: Yeah that's right. We saw a 3x increase in inference traffic for our shipments summarization flow, so our current dedicated pool is getting saturated during peak windows. Also EU customers are reporting 150-200ms higher tail latency, so adding a Frankfurt region would really help.
[00:40] Ravi: Quick clarifying q — are you looking to add full dedicated capacity in EU or a smaller reserve with failover?
[00:45] Priya: Ideally full capacity — we want consistent SLAs across regions. But we also need to balance cost. If there's a cheaper warm-standby approach that's acceptable as long as failover is near-instant.
[00:56] Jamie: Ok. We typically offer either dedicated GPU pools (reserved) in the region, or a cross-region routing policy with a warm-burst pool that can spin up. Reserved gives predictable latency and cost but is a higher commit. Warm-standby is cheaper but you get a small increase in cold-start or warm-up latency.
[01:12] Tom: Can you share what predictability looks like? Like percentiles on latency for reserved v. warm?
[01:17] Ravi: Sure. For reserved on our M60-style profile — you're looking at median latencies consistent with your baseline, tail p95/p99 is much tighter. For warm-standby, p95 can be 1.2-1.5x during burst while caches (KV cache) warm. Note: SE audio transcript says "K V cash" sometimes, sorry.
[01:33] Priya: And about cost — can you show a 12 month commit vs month-to-month? Our procurement needs options.
[01:38] Jamie: Absolutely — I'll send 3 pricing options: hosted overage, dedicated reserved monthly commit, and a dedicated + extra region reserved bundle with discount for multi-region commit.
[01:48] Sophie: Procurement will likely push for a 12 month term, but need to see the price bands. Also need SOC 2 and encryption details for legal.
[01:56] Lena: We can share SOC 2 report, and we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and keys for Dedicated. We also provide audit logs and retention options.
[02:05] Tom: On networking — we need VPC peering and private endpoints. How does Redwood handle private deployments?
[02:12] Jamie: For Private/VPC we provide a private control plane and customer-managed networking — VPC peering or transit gateway is doable. For Dedicated hosted in a cloud region, we can set up S3/VPC endpoints and restrict egress. There is also an on-prem option if required, but that is heavier.
[02:28] Markus: We'll probably stick to cloud VPC peering for now. We need to confirm data residency for logs and encryption at rest.
[02:35] Ravi: We can scope that — logs can be sent to your customer logging account or we can retain them in region. For encryption at rest we support provider KMS. There's some nuance with audit log retention windows if you need long-term retention — that is an add-on.
[02:49] Markus: Another ask — can you run a run-rate perf test with our real prompt set? We want to see 99th pct latency numbers for 1k and 2k qps.
[02:57] Ravi: Yep, that's something we do. If you share the prompt files and a test token and expected seq lengths, we can run it on a reserved profile mirroring the capacity you're considering. I'll note that as an action.
[03:07] Priya: Also curious about model fallbacks — if we're on a specific quantized variant for cost, does Redwood automatically fall back to a full-precision host in outages?
[03:15] Ravi: We support routing policies that can fall back to compatible model variants or a hosted-grade model. There's a config for cost-aware routing and also a safety net so you don't get 503s. Fallbacks are configurable per-route.
[03:25] Tom: For contract extension, we need to know how pricing scales if we add the EU region later — do you allow retroactive region adds mid-term?
[03:33] Jamie: Yes, you can add regions mid-term; pricing will be pro-rated, and if you commit to a longer term with multi-region reserved, we can apply an additional discount. We'll show both an add-on price and a bundled multi-region discount in the quote.
[03:45] Sophie: Timeline: procurement approval takes about 4-6 weeks internally. We're aiming to have contractual terms signed by end of July. Is that feasible?
[03:54] Jamie: Totally — sounds feasible. We'll need to get pricing and security artifacts to you ASAP.
[03:58] Markus: One more technical — on caching: do you offer prefix / KV cache warming during migration so that tail latency doesn't spike?
[04:05] Ravi: Yes, we have prefix caching and KV cache migration tooling. We can preload commonly used keys into the cache during cutover. Also batching strategies help reduce cost while keeping latency within SLOs.
[04:17] Priya: Speaking of batching — what's your guidance for our mix of short vs long prompts? Our homegrown NLG is mostly short summaries but sometimes long-blow transcripts for customer disputes.
[04:26] Ravi: For mixed profiles we recommend a hybrid: smaller batch sizes for low-latency paths and queued batching for large-batch offline workflows. Redwood Optimize can run an analysis against your prompt set to recommend quantization and batching profiles.
[04:38] Jamie: Ok quick recap — action items and timelines: I'll send pricing/options and contract term scenarios; Ravi will run perf benchmarks; Tom will send infra diagram; Sophie will confirm procurement timeline. We'll schedule a technical deep dive the week of 6/29.
[04:52] Sophie: Sounds good.
[04:54] Markus: One ask — can you also include a cost projection for 12 months at our forecasted growth rates? That will help finance.
[05:02] Jamie: Yup we'll include a 12-month TCO with growth assumptions and a sensitivity table.
[05:07] Priya: And please include SLA details for p95 and p99 latency for the reserved option.
[05:12] Lena: We'll include SLO/SLA targets per route and dedicated pool in the docs.
[05:18] Tom: Ok thanks everyone, looking forward to the perf results.
[05:21] Jamie: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials.

Notes / imperfections: occasional speaker mislabels (often 'Speaker 2' in transit), a few transcription errors — e.g., "KV cache" appears as "K V cash" and "Redwood Dedicated" appears as "Redwood Dedicate" in one segment. References shared: pricing sheet (link: /redwood/quotes/CRM-45871), SOC2 report (shared), perf template spreadsheet (shared).

End of call.
